fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Breaking the Addiction to Fear", "body": "Beth Martens opens by describing how hard it is to deliver good news, saying listeners grow addicted to the adrenaline of famine and dollar collapse stories. Brandon Sterling recalls shows where the more data he presented, the more people clung to collapse narratives, and he argues that gold and silver are not the safe harbor many in the alternative space believe. Beth credits Brandon and Clint Richardson with freeing her from expecting the world to end, and the conversation agrees that work is far more enjoyable once that fear lifts."}, {"title": "Questioning the 508 C1A Pitch", "body": "Brandon walks through what he calls the most popular myth in the private realm, the idea that a 508 C1A is a tax free entity outside IRS reach. In his reading, it is only a section of the tax code describing how 501c3 organizations relate to exemption, not a structure anyone can form. He points to the IRS fourteen point church checklist, Taylor versus Commissioner and a client's EIN letter as support. Beth adds that naming her own association a ministry, on someone's advice, ended up drawing attention rather than deflecting it."}, {"title": "The Private Is Simply Life", "body": "Brandon argues that private associations are older than nonprofits and already exist in nature, citing families, historical societies, HOAs and even the Bar Association as examples. He says you do not need a PMA to give vegetables to neighbors or shovel driveways. Chance frames the real trouble as people mixing up their straw man corporate identity with their true self, and Brandon agrees the goal is separating what you hold from your public name. Chance also suggests the only full escape from taxation is living with as little commerce as possible."}, {"title": "Owning Nothing, Controlling Everything", "body": "Brandon presents his toolkit of LLCs, private associations and trusts, describing an LLC as a separate person that handles commerce and liability so the individual does not. He contrasts living trusts with irrevocable trusts, argues that wills invite probate and creditor claims, and sketches roadmaps where a holding company and an irrevocable trust sit above a business. He frames all of this as structure that should be done legitimately and transparently, and he closes by telling listeners to find a good CPA for their own tax accounting rather than relying on him."}, {"title": "Currency as Current and Life Force", "body": "Chance reflects that no one can leave nature or lose God given rights, and argues wealth is not a zero sum game. He links currency to current, saying money flow mirrors how well a person's life force is integrated, and recalls biofield tuning clients who reported unexpected repayments after sessions. Beth describes deprogramming as defragmenting competing inner parts and tells how fear gave way to building her Journey Code Coaching Certification. Brandon adds his view that money is energy that never disappears, only transfers, so the work is learning which side of it to stand on."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Brandon Sterling of Safe Haven Co. joins Vibe Rant to help us comprehend the ins and outs of setting up a PMA (Private Member Association) to protect and preserve our private and innate God given rights. Through his work at Safe Haven Co., Brandon helps people become Un-Collectable, by owning nothing, and controlling everything.
